rules.title: Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing Ordinance (proposed)
rules.requirement: Would make it unlawful for any person to sell, license or otherwise provide an algorithmic device to a landlord, and unlawful for a landlord to use one to set rental rates or occupancy levels. An algorithmic device is software that uses nonpublic competitor data to advise or recommend rents or occupancy levels; reports based on public data or on aggregated data more than 90 days old, and affordable-housing program tools, are excluded.
rules.key_value: Ban on sale, licensing and use of algorithmic rent-setting devices; civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation
rules.citation: Proposed San Diego Municipal Code ch. 9, art. 8, div. 11, §§98.1101-98.1104 (O-2025-107)
rules.quoted_span:
It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates
or occupancy levels for residential rental property.
rules.coverage_text: Residential rental property in the City of San Diego; applies to any person selling, licensing or providing an algorithmic device to a landlord and to landlords using one.
rules.exemptions: Software or products that publish reports on rental rates or occupancy levels from aggregated historical nonpublic competitor data more than 90 days old, or from information available to the general public, and that do not recommend rates or occupancy levels for future leases or renewals. Software or products used to set rental rates or income limits under local, state or federal affordable housing program guidelines.
rules.penalty: A tenant may sue a landlord for injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation. A prevailing tenant recovers costs and reasonable attorney's fees, and lease clauses limiting fee recovery are unenforceable. Each month of use, and each property where a device is used, is a separate violation. Remedies are cumulative.
rules.extraction_note: Document is a staff report (Feb 27, 2025) with a draft ordinance whose ordinance number, date of final passage, adoption date and mayoral approval/veto lines are blank, so it is treated as pending. The draft states it would take effect on the thirtieth day after final passage, but no passage date is given, so effective_date and enacted_date are left blank. City Attorney approval is dated November 14, 2024.
